Explore the unique world of altitude diving, where you’ll learn crucial skills for high-altitude environments and deepen your understanding of decompression theory.
Practice hands-on buoyancy techniques, from weight adjustments to fine-tuning breath control, under the guidance of an instructor.
In small group sessions, you’ll cover essential topics like the physiological effects of altitude, equipment adjustments, and using the Recreational Dive Planner at higher elevations. {"redo_desc_about":"Enjoy a choice of two reef locations, classic yacht and a friendly professional team to look after you
You are in for an exceptional Great Barrier Reef adventure with Rum Runner who specializes in Cairns Great Barrier Reef experiences, catering to swimmers and snorkelers, those wanting to try an introductory dive (no experience necessary) and certified scuba divers of all experience levels.
2 different dive and snorkel sites
Special Prices start from $220.00
Returns to Cairns at 6pm
Each site your dive will be unique, allowing you to explore vast coral gardens, walls and isolated pinnacles, while amazing you with the sheer diversity and colour of marine life. Rum Runner offers you the freedom to dive with your buddy or join a guided dive with one of our dive crew at no extra cost!
During your Rum Runner full day tour, you have the option of taking up to two dives at the two reef sites we visit. The first site allows for unlimited snorkel and dive time of up to 120 minutes. If you can make your tank last that long, go for it! Or if you’re quick on your air, come back for a short refill and jump back in. We will let you know what time you need to be back for lunch.
The second site we visit is a unique Sand Cay in the middle of a vast Coral Garden. Dive here or snorkel over to the cay and walk on a sand island in the middle of the ocean.
Tour includes dive quality masks and fins. Wetsuits are available in all sizes and include 3mm full length.
Rum Runner offers a tanks and weight rate for Scuba divers bringing their own scuba equipment. Top quality scuba equipment, including dive computers available for hire.
Departing 3pm from the sand cay, enjoy a relaxing sunset sail and cruise on deck. BYO your own beer and wine. {"redo_desc_about":"Please arrive by 9:40 AM for a mandatory 20-minute safety briefing. The tour starts promptly at 10:00 AM and takes around two hours.
Embark on a scenic e-bike tour to explore the Noosa North Shore Wilderness Trail. This journey includes a picturesque ferry crossing and rides through iconic local landmarks.
The Noosa North Shore is part of a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, teeming with native fauna. Keep an eye out for:
Land Species: Kangaroos, koalas echidnas, possums, and various bird species like glossy black cockatoos and white-bellied sea eagles.
Marine Life: Explore coastal areas where you might spot reef fish, bottlenose dolphins, and loggerhead turtles.
Noosa National Park: A short distance from Hastings Street, this park is a great spot to see koalas, wallabies, and more.
The tour concludes with a return ride along the same picturesque route, giving you another chance to soak in the stunning river views and lush landscapes.","redo_desc_important_info":"","redo_desc_highlights":"Gympie Terrace: Enjoy a ride along the vibrant Noosa River, offering serene views and a lively atmosphere perfect for outdoor enthusiasts. Experience the local culture with various dining options and outdoor activities.

Moorindil Street Ferry: Board the ferry that connects the mainland to Noosa North Shore. This ferry has been a lifeline for the area, evolving from a modest barge to a robust dual-ferry operation crucial for accessing the local natural attractions.

{"redo_desc_about":"Experience the joy of shaping hot metal on a traditional Blacksmith’s anvil and under a power hammer.
It's a PRIVATE experience so you will not be in with random people, it's just you and whoever you book with.
We provide all the equipment, materials and safety gear
You get to take home everything you make
You will get the chance to hand forge a variety of products and generally experience the joy of shaping hot metal on a traditional Blacksmith’s anvil and under a power hammer. You get to take home various products that you have made from scratch and they will be talking pieces for years to come.
Be prepared to get your hands dirty, with this very ‘hands on’ experience, forging metal objects from upcycled materials. I will be there assisting you, one-on-one, helping you understand the art of raw blacksmithing.
No experience needed however it will definitely be helpful if you are comfortable using power tools, I will instruct you carefully and demonstrate the safe use of the tools and machinery, some of which you probably wouldn't have encountered before.
The main tools and machines used are:
A forge for heating the steel
An anvil and hand hammer
A power hammer
Angle grinders (cutting and surface grinding)
A belt grinder, sometimes known as a linisher
Wire wheel on a bench grinder
UPDATE JULY 1st 2025 - New Legislation around Swords
Due to unexpected new legislation in South Australia, it is now unfortunately illegal for us to offer sword-making, even during private workshops. The penalties for breaching this law are extremely harsh - up to 2 years in jail and a $20,000 fine - so while this is frustrating and disappointing, it’s simply not something we can risk.
Although there is no minimum age limit to participate in our Blacksmith Experiences, participants under the age of 18 may take part in knife-making activities only under the direct supervision of a parent or legal guardian.
If a participant under 18 creates a knife during a workshop, an adult must be present in order for the finished item to be taken home.
Without a supervising adult present, the knife will remain on-site and held for collection by a parent or guardian.
This policy ensures compliance with South Australian regulations and helps us maintain a safe and responsible workshop environment for all participants.","redo_desc_important_info":"If you wish to make a larger item like a Cleaver or Pizza Cutter or any wooden handled knives from our website you will need to book a FULL DAY experience due to the duration of the heat treatment. A maximum of 2 larger items can be made in one full day.
For the safety of our guests and staff, Bushy’s Projects does not operate blacksmithing experiences on days where the forecast temperature is above 32°C. Working with hot steel and an open forge in extreme heat creates unsafe conditions, so sessions will be postponed or rescheduled if this limit is exceeded.
If a day is forecast to reach over 32°C, we will contact all bookings as early as possible to arrange an alternative date or discuss available options. Your safety and comfort are always our top priority, and we appreciate your understanding in helping us maintain a safe and enjoyable experience for everyone.","redo_desc_highlights":"","redo_desc_what_included":"","redo_desc_what_excluded":"","redo_desc_extras":"","redo_desc_itinerary":"","redo_desc_what_to_bring":"","redo_desc_duration_text":"Up To 4 Hours

{"redo_desc_about":"A different fun and exciting class for your kids!
Menu: Seasonal Fruit Smoothies; Bread Rolls; Baked Egg & Bacon Muffins, Chicken Puff Pies; Cheat Chocolate Eclairs and Fruit Pavlovas!
Drop the kids off and let them loose in the kitchen with us whilst you enjoy a relaxing morning out chatting over coffee or getting a few things done - kid free!
In this exciting hands-on kids cooking class your kids will be guided by our 2 Chefs to learn how to work in teams with some tasks allocated individually to each child, and be taught how to prepare some great, fun and tactile food that they can replicate at home.
This is such a tactile and entertaining class that the kids won't even realise that they are gaining valuable life skills.

{"redo_desc_about":"The Supper Club at Hapuku Kitchen offers a unique dining experience in our home, inspired by nature's larder
Join us for dinner celebrating foraged and sustainably farmed produce from the wild environment of Kaikōura, New Zealand, prepared and cooked in our kitchen at the base of the world.
Our three-course, set menus are a celebration of the season and everything the region has to offer.
Our dining table seats twelve guests and while you're savouring the flavours of Kaikōura, you'll hear stories about how we grow our food, how we forage from the mountains to the sea and the people behind locally sourced ingredients.
We focus on ingredients we have grown ourselves, foraged or sourced from our neighbours. Everything is made from scratch and the menu is finalised the day prior, based on what is at its absolute best.
Get a group of friends or family together and book the entire table of twelve, or book a seat and meet other people interested in good food and great company.
It's a good question. Supper clubs are places for people to enjoy fine, high-quality food, without formalities. Many supper clubs are hosted by people in their own houses, so it feels as though you're visiting them for dinner.
A supper club really can be anything, with many taking the form of pop-up concepts and even underground restaurants. Typically there is no choice when it comes to the menu, and the whole thing has a more relaxed, communal feeling when compared to a restaurant.

About - Introduction to Stained Glass
Curious about stained glass? Join us for an introductory two day stained glass workshop with visiting UK glass artist Jan Simpson. Perfect for beginners wanting to explore the art of stained glass, you will learn foundational techniques for working with stained glass including glass cutting, soldering, cementing and polishing.
What you’ll do
Over two days, you’ll create a stained glass panel using leaded techniques. You’ll have a choice of two designs, each offering a different set of challenges to help you understand how to approach your own original designs in future. This workshop is suitable for a complete beginner, or those ready to build on previous experience.
- Approach and create a design in glass
- Measure, cut, and handle glass safely
- Select and cut coloured glass pieces
- Lead, solder, cement, and polish your finished stained glass panel
The completed panel will be taken home by the student for final polishing up at home once the cement has dried. A demonstration of this will be shown at the end of the day and a fully written handout will be supplied to each student for them to take away for future reference.
About the Artist
Jan Simpson is a UK-based glass artist with over 30 years of experience, specializing in bespoke stained and fused glass. Originally from New Zealand, she blends traditional, heritage craftsmanship with contemporary techniques to explore light, colour, and form. Jan works to commission and teaches from her Bognor Regis studio.
Objective
Students will learn shop safety, be introduced to the shop, tools, materials and techniques used in stained glass. Students will have the opportunity to apply those skills to create their very own using the techniques taught in the class. {"redo_desc_about":"We travel along a less traveled part of Lake Burley Griffin to view the Governor General's residence from the lake. It provides an other perspective on your National Capital. We also present a different angle on the areas history which is not usually covered on our one hour tours. A complementary light morning tea is provided on this cruise.
We take you to see the Governor Generals' residence from the lake and present a well researched commentary on some of the early European history of the area. Our guests are frequently surprised about some of the information we share on this cruise. 
Join us for a relaxing leisurely cruise along a section of the lake which is less frequently traveled. The area has an amassing history, of both the original indigenous folk and the early European settlers.

The owner and operator of Lake Burley Griffin Cruises is Jim Paterson, who has lived in Canberra with his wife Virginia since the early 1980s. Jim had a long and successful career in broadcasting and television before turning his attention to the water in 2003. His entertaining and well-researched commentary is one of the highlights of your lake cruise. The Boats;Our first boat Cygnet was converted from the steam launch Jenny and commenced service in 2003. It’s a replica Edwardian style electric launch. Cygnet was the first commercial all electric vessel on Lake Burley Griffin, and the uniquely quiet ride adds an extra element of tranquillity to the cruise. The MV Gull commenced service in October 2009, increasing the passenger carrying capacity and enhancing our range of services. In 2012 Gull was converted to all electric. Both electric boats are running on green energy charging their batteries overnight. {"redo_desc_about":"A quick sampler flight into the Kepler Mountains - with Fiordland tarns and breathtaking lake views

{"redo_desc_about":"Departing Sydney at 0600 and only 90 minutes from Sydney, the Central coast has some beautiful habitats and bird species not found so easily in Sydney. Ourimbah Rest Stop is a great place to start. We look for Bassian Thrush, Regent Bowerbird, Green Catbird, Yellow-throated Scrubwren and other rainforest species.
We then head off to Central Coast Wetlands (Pioneer Dairy) where over 230 species have been recorded, including a variety of waterbirds and Red-rumped Parrots. Tuggerah Wetlands is close by and has a variety of waterbirds as is McPherson Road Swamp, where we may see the giant Black-necked Stocrk.
Palmdale is an exciting stop for Australian Logrunner, Noisy Pitta, Rose Robin and White-headed Pigeon.
Final stop is St Huberts Island to locate the elusive Bush Stone-curlew.

Expect to identify 80+species.
Arrive back in Sydney around 1800.

{"redo_desc_about":"Experience two iconic NZ visitor attractions in one amazing day starting in Rotorua and ending in Auckland. See the iconic Hobbiton Movie Set, the world-famous Waitomo Glowworm Caves and travel through the beautiful Waikato region.

After pick-up in Rotorua, we drive across the Mamaku Plateau to the Hobbiton Movie Set near the rural town of Matamata, made world-famous as the original setting of Sir Peter Jackson’s “The Lord of the Rings” and “The Hobbit” trilogies. On the 2-hour tour of the Hobbiton Movie Set, get astonishing insights into how these movies were made and which parts of the movies were filmed here. Not only movie fans will enjoy this unique experience with inside views of the Hobbit village including Hobbit Holes, Bag End, The Green Dragon Inn and astonishing facts about the filmmaking and spectacular landscape all around.
We then continue on to Waitomo Caves, located in the King Country in the Waikato region. On this tour we travel via the Thermal Explorer Highway touring route, taking in the special region as we drive through the beautiful countryside of New Zealand’s North Island. At Waitomo, experience the underground wonderland that is Waitomo Glowworm Caves with thousands of Glowworms as the major attraction.
As we drive northward on the journey from Waitomo to Auckland, we show you sacred Taupiri Mountain as well as Ngaruawahia, the site of Turangawaewae Marae (Maori meeting place) and seat of New Zealand’s Maori King. {"redo_desc_about":"Nothing tastes better than fruit picked straight from the tree - and we’ll show you why in our Pick Your Own persimmon experience.

{"redo_desc_about":"Giiyong | Welcome - to Thaua Country!
Connect to Country along a 3.8km trail that is part of the Gateway to the Bundian Way, where ancient stories, ceremony, breathtaking landscapes, and Aboriginal culture come alive.
Begin with a traditional smoking ceremony at Jigamy, home to the Keeping Place, before venturing along a section of the Bundian Way to the breathtaking geological feature, the Pinnacles. Traverse serene coastal bushlands that open to sweeping ocean vistas, guided by Country Custodians who share their deep connection to the land. Immerse yourself in the rich knowledge systems of the local Aboriginal community, learning about plants, cultural practices, and the timeless ways of knowing that have sustained this land for thousands of years. This is more than a guided walk; it’s a profound cultural experience.
By participating in this cultural tour operated by the Eden Local Aboriginal Land Council, you are helping to make a difference in our local community. Incredible Cultural Knowledge
Be guided by a Country Custodian and hear stories of survival, tradition, and deep connection to Country, passed down for thousands of years. Learn about cultural practices, knowledge systems, and the enduring relationship between people and Country.
Diverse and Ancient Landscapes

{"redo_desc_about":"Guided Heli-Fishing
Experience the ultimate fishing adventure
Fishing like never before with a Heli-fishing adventure that takes you to the most pristine, remote locations only accessible by helicopter. Soar over rugged landscapes, vast forests, and crystal-clear waters as you’re transported to hidden fishing spots teeming with fish. With unparalleled access to secluded coastlines, you’ll have the chance to cast your line in untouched, trophy-worthy waters.
Where the journey is as epic as the catch
$5,995 up to 5 people
Departing from North Shore Airport, Auckland, you'll fly over the stunning islands of the Hauraki Gulf, taking in a bird’s-eye view of the dramatic land and seascape below before landing at either Great Barrier Island or the Coromandel.

After around four hours of fishing, we’ll lift off again and make our way back to Auckland, soaring over the same breathtaking landscapes—returning with your well-earned catch.
We’ll supply everything you need for a great day on the water: Daiwa graphite rods and premium spinning reels, and all the tackle and bait required.
Chilled bottled water and a classic fisherman’s lunch are all part of the package. Feel free to request specific foods and drinks if you’d like to enhance the experience.
The full experience takes around 5 to 6 hours and departure times vary depending on the tide.

Chocolate factory
Free tasting 3 different flavoured chocolate while you explore the venue. Try the creamy ice cream, hot or cold chocolate drink, a cup of coffee or a snack to satisfy your appetite.
Morish Nuts
Munch the samples at Morish Nuts, which produces a variety of nuts flavored with caramel, wasabi, spices, abalone, and more.
Mondo Nougat factory
Sample the Italian-style soft nougat at the Mondo Nougat factory.
Honey and Wine Tasting
Experience a variety of honey in the Honey House. You’ll also visit renowned vineyards in the Swan Valley for wine tastings.
Aboriginal Culture Experience
peruse the Maalinup Aboriginal Gallery to learn about aboriginal history and culture, and sample traditional bush food.
Great Coffee experience

{"redo_desc_about":"Join us for a unique and exclusive Wellington sightseeing experience.
Shenandoah, one of our favourite Wellington tours and exclusive to Xplor Tours, takes you to perhaps the best but least known destination in the region.

Approximately 20 minutes’ drive from Wellington, overlooking the sparkling Pauatahanui Inlet and linked with Battle Hill (a significant Maori War site), Shenandoah is a working farm and hidden historical gem inside a native wild birdlife reserve.

Once Xplor Tours drops you there, owner and proud Kiwi Simon takes you on a unique and magical tour around his beautiful, relaxing property, and through its history.

Originally a Maori Fortress Pa for Ngati Toa in the 1800’s, the property has seen three different owners over 150 years. After withstanding a major battle with English troops, it became a Crown Fort to guard the stagecoach road from highway robbers. Some of the first settlers to New Zealand made contact with the local iwi here, before the whalers and settlers transformed Pauatahanui into the thriving rural community of today.

Early in World War II, Shenandoah was commandeered as a US Marine training base and housed over 100,000 troops, ushering in the next military episode of the site.

The history isn’t just told in stories though; behind the barn doors, a private museum is filled with artifacts found on the property which date back over the last 150 years.

As part of your day trip to Shenandoah with Xplor Tours, you can relax by the pond and jetty or other seating areas in the gardens, and enjoy a tea or coffee with morning or afternoon tea.

Simon’s passion and ability to enthral makes this Wellington tour experience genuinely unique and one that will stay with you long after you leave Shenandoah.

Come on a Shenandoah tour with Xplor Tours and you will see why “Pauatahanui” means “the place you never want to leave from.”","redo_desc_important_info":"We don’t want to spoil all the surprises, but this is the Wellington tour to do if you want to experience any or all of the following:

{"redo_desc_about":"In this new series of weeknight masterclasses we're luring some exciting chef talent out of their restaurants and into the Sydney Seafood School kitchen.
Seafood specialist and head chef at North Bondi Fish, David Coumont's cooking is guided by simplicity, seasonality, respect for produce and a desire to showcase lesser-known seafood species.
Originally trained as a graphic designer, David changed direction in his late twenties and began his culinary training in Belgium. His first restaurant role was at Bozar in Brussels, now a two-Michelin-star restaurant. He went on to gain experience at leading European kitchens, including Maison Bras in Laguiole, before moving to Australia. In Sydney, he worked at The Woods, Fish Face alongside Stephen Hodges and Josh Niland, then spent time at Café Paci.
In 2015, he opened Moxhe in Bronte, a small seafood-focused restaurant inspired by Australian produce and his Belgian background. At Moxhe, David visited the Sydney Fish Market each morning and adapted the menu around the best seasonal fish available that day. After eight years at Moxhe, he became Head Chef of North Bondi Fish, bringing his market-driven seafood approach to one of Sydney’s best-known beachside restaurants.
This class will celebrate the diversity of Australian seafood in a way that is fresh, relaxed and deeply connected to the ocean. {"redo_desc_about":"The Real Sydney Starts Here
Forget the postcards — this isn’t polished Sydney. This is the real story, and it starts in The Rocks.
Once a wild colonial outpost built on stolen land, The Rocks was carved out by convicts, ruled by rum, and soaked in scandal. On this 2.5-hour walking tour, you’ll trace the strange and staggering birth of modern Sydney — where the world’s oldest living culture collided with the most outrageous maritime gamble in British history.
Wander crooked lanes and cobbled streets. Hear true stories of escapes, disasters, ghost alleys, and the underground stream still
running beneath your feet. Along the way, you’ll sample native bush flavours — like wattle seed tea and Davidson’s plum jam — for a literal taste of the land and its stories.
No boring lectures — just bloody interesting yarns told with heart and humour","redo_desc_important_info":"","redo_desc_highlights":"","redo_desc_what_included":"","redo_desc_what_excluded":"","redo_desc_extras":"","redo_desc_itinerary":"","redo_desc_what_to_bring":"","redo_desc_duration_text":"","redo_desc_cancellation":"","redo_desc_check_in":"","redo_desc_accessibility":"","redo_desc_restrictions":"","redo_desc_special_requirements":"","redo_desc_faqs":"","redo_desc_pricing":"","redo_desc_disclaimers":"","redo_meeting_point":"","redo_min_age":"","redo_max_age":"","redo_group_size":"","redo_flags":""}

{"redo_desc_about":"Up Close With New Zealand’s Stunning Natural Beauty
Departure Time- 7:30am inside Port Chalmers or from all centrally located accommodation.
Departure times can vary depending on the arrival/departure times of visiting cruise ships and will be confirmed during the booking process. If you have any concerns please contact us
Return Time- 5:30pm
Sparsely populated - save for the wildlife who call this rugged coastline home - the Catlins in the southern tip of the South Island offers views of some of New Zealand’s most stunning natural beauty.

Your tour begins at 8am from your accommodation as we head south along the Southern Scenic route, through the sea-side village of Brighton before stopping for photos at the mouth of the mighty Taieri River. Continuing on you will go through Waihola and Balclutha before arriving in Owaka, the gateway to the Catlins. Your first short walk takes you to Nugget Point, the most iconic landform of the Otago Coastline. From here you will see the several rugged rocks likened to gold nuggets where NZ fur seals and many NZ seabirds can be viewed. If you visit between December and February there is always the chance of seeing a huge Elephant Seal from the viewing platform. Continuing south our next stop is at a picturesque bay known to be a favourite haul-out site for the rarest sea lion in the world, the New Zealand sea lion. After being hunted to near extinction, only about 200 remain on the mainland. Stand in awe of their magnificence, you’ll be as close as 10 metres from one of these wonderful marine mammals.

Driving through native coastal rainforest surrounded by ancient trees your next short walk takes you to the highest waterfall in the Catlins. Your guide will introduce you to several native bush birds and native plants before you arrive at the McLean Falls, arguably the most spectacular of all the waterfalls in the Catlins. Further south you will get the opportunity to look for one of the rarest and smallest dolphins in the world – the Hectors dolphin. The nutrient-rich waters attract this dolphin to become resident in one of the bays on the Catlins coast during the warmer months. You will be taken to the best vantage points to look for these dolphins while you guide prepares light refreshments.

Your last stop is at a 180 million year old petrified forest that is revealed at low tide. The fossilised remains of an ancient forest can clearly be seen, representing one of only three accessible sites in the world. {"redo_desc_about":"Embark on an immersive journey through the stunning landscapes of the Hauraki Coromandel Peninsula, where natural beauty meets Māori cultural heritage. Starting with a pick-up from the Matariki Tours Hub at 150 Pound Street, Coromandel, guests will set off on a scenic round-trip along the western coast of the peninsula to Colville, where they can relax and enjoy morning tea at the charming Pickled Hereford Café.
The adventure continues as we cross the majestic Coromandel Ranges, offering breathtaking views of Moehau (Tūpuna Maunga) while traveling through Waikawau Bay, Little Bay, and Tuateawa on the peninsula’s eastern side. Upon arrival at Tokatea Maunga, guests will be treated to a presentation overlooking the stunning Hauraki Gulf. Here, a knowledgeable kaikorero (speaker) will guide them through the history and significance of the surrounding landscape and the cultural landmarks, providing a deep insight into the Māori worldview and local traditions.
During this experience, guests will participate in workshops that bring ancient Māori customs to life, gaining hands-on insights into practices such as Rongoā Māori (traditional healing). Through captivating storytelling, the kaikorero will reveal the significance of Matariki (the Māori New Year) and share the profound connection Māori culture holds with "Papatūānuku" (Mother Earth), "Ranginui" (Father Sky), and "Tikapa Moana" (the ancestral ocean).
Afterward, guests will be transported back to Coromandel Town, where they can explore local shops and enjoy the vibrant hospitality scene. This tour offers an ideal blend of adventure, cultural enrichment, and the chance to experience the charm of Coromandel’s community firsthand.","redo_desc_important_info":"","redo_desc_highlights":"","redo_desc_what_included":"","redo_desc_what_excluded":"","redo_desc_extras":"","redo_desc_itinerary":"","redo_desc_what_to_bring":"","redo_desc_duration_text":"","redo_desc_cancellation":"","redo_desc_check_in":"","redo_desc_accessibility":"","redo_desc_restrictions":"","redo_desc_special_requirements":"","redo_desc_faqs":"","redo_desc_pricing":"","redo_desc_disclaimers":"","redo_meeting_point":"","redo_min_age":"","redo_max_age":"","redo_group_size":"","redo_flags":""}

{"redo_desc_about":"Discover Wallagoot Lake at Night
Our Night Kayaking Tour is the Sapphire Coast's best kept secret. Discover the magic and adventure of night kayaking on the tranquil and protected Wallagoot lake. Just a short drive from Merimbula (20 minutes) and Tathra (15 minutes), this tour offers a truly unique perspective on the natural world.
We'll begin at the Wallagoot Lake Sailing Club and prepare for our night adventure. As we paddle toward the mouth of the lake, you'll glide through a beautiful wetland area bustling with seabirds like pelicans, black swans, cormorants, and sea eagles. The sandy dunes along the shore are a great spot to see kangaroos as they come out to graze at dusk.
After enjoying sunset, we'll stop for a delicious supper on the shore. You'll feast on a platter featuring local Tilba cheese, crackers, and seasonal fruit, along with a selection of hot drinks and orange juice.
As the sun disappears and the stars begin to emerge, we'll make our way back. This is when the lake truly comes alive. Listen for the chorus of frogs and the rustle of evening birds. Using our special underwater light, we'll search for fish, prawns, jellyfish, and even stingrays in the shallow, protected waters below. With lights on each kayak, we'll paddle safely back together, savouring this surreal and serene experience.
The timing of this tour varies with the seasons, as it's perfectly timed to coincide with the sunset. This makes for a later start in the summer, but a fantastic experience for the entire family.

The Yarra Valley is one of several wine destinations in Australia however unique in the fact that it is home to well known Domaine Chandon in Australia. Enjoy a private wine tasting in the famous Green Room situated inside Domaine, or visit any number of other boutique and organic world class cellar doors. Your private guide will tailor an authentic experience to suit you.

One of our first winery stops for the day will be at Coldstream Hills. With a reputation for producing outstanding single vineyard and reserve wines Coldstream Hills has a particular focus on the internationally heralded varieties, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. Next we’ll go to Domaine Chandon – established by French champagne house Moët & Chandon in 1986, this scenic winery set amongst the verdant hills of the Yarra Valley is dedicated to traditional production methods of cool climate still wines.

Lunch today is at Yering Station. Set within stunning architecture, this signature restaurant overlooks expansive and magnificent views of the Yarra Ranges. Yering Station’s Head Chef, Laura Webb-James, designs tempting menus making the most of the fresh, seasonal produce available from the region. The afternoon will be ours to enjoy. The Waitomo Caves, which are located about 2 ½ hours south of Auckland, is one of New Zealand’s most famous attractions. On this tour we travel via New Zealand’s famous Thermal Explorer Highway touring route, taking in the special region of Hamilton through the beautiful countryside of the Waikato and King Country.

As we drive southward, we show you sacred Taupiri Mountain as well as Ngaruawahia, the site of the famous Turangawaewae Marae (Maori meeting place) and seat of New Zealand’s Maori King. At Waitomo you will experience one of their amazing tours to explore the underground wonderland that is Waitomo Caves. The most popular option is the world-famous Waitomo Glowworm Caves on a 45 minute tour, which includes a boat ride on an underground stream to view the magically dazzling glowworms. There are other caving options too, such as Cave Tubing / Black Water Rafting. Here you can float, walk and swim along underground waterways on a big, inflated tube. {"redo_desc_about":"Do Tricks At Manly Beach!
Riding a trick skateboard is an exhilarating experience that combines balance, agility, and creativity. Designed specifically for performing tricks, these skateboards feature smaller, harder wheels and narrower decks compared to cruisers or longboards. These characteristics make trick skateboards ideal for technical manoeuvres like ollies, flips, grinds, and aerial tricks, especially in skate parks and urban environments.
The first step in mastering a trick skateboard is building a solid foundation in balance and control. Learning how to properly stand on the deck, control your speed, and steer using your body weight are essential skills. Once comfortable, riders can begin practising basic tricks like the ollie, which is the foundation of many more advanced tricks. An ollie allows skaters to lift the board off the ground without using their hands and is crucial for jumps and aerial stunts.
As riders progress, they can experiment with more advanced tricks like kickflips, where the skateboard rotates underfoot while airborne, or grinding on rails and ledges. Each trick requires precise foot placement and timing, demanding hours of practice to perfect. Skating on smooth surfaces like concrete in skate parks or streets is ideal for these types of tricks, as hard wheels give better speed and control on such surfaces.
In addition to technique, riding a trick skateboard also emphasises creativity and personal style. Skaters often combine tricks, develop their own variations, and find unique spots in urban landscapes to showcase their skills. The individuality of skating is a big part of its appeal, making it more than just a sport, but a form of self-expression.
Overall, riding a trick skateboard requires patience, practice, and persistence, but the rewards are immense. It’s a challenging, dynamic sport that continually pushes your limits, offering an ever-evolving sense of accomplishment and fun.","redo_desc_important_info":"","redo_desc_highlights":"","redo_desc_what_included":"","redo_desc_what_excluded":"","redo_desc_extras":"","redo_desc_itinerary":"","redo_desc_what_to_bring":"","redo_desc_duration_text":"","redo_desc_cancellation":"","redo_desc_check_in":"","redo_desc_accessibility":"","redo_desc_restrictions":"","redo_desc_special_requirements":"","redo_desc_faqs":"","redo_desc_pricing":"","redo_desc_disclaimers":"","redo_meeting_point":"","redo_min_age":"","redo_max_age":"","redo_group_size":"","redo_flags":""}

{"redo_desc_about":"Discover Tasmania’s hidden gem—Leven Canyon: epic views, fresh mountain air, and a scenic escape just a short walk away!
